release_rule: Every mandatory check must pass. No averaging, no approval on retry exhaustion.

checks.name: Complete lesson structure
checks.pass: All required lesson sections, a complete worked example, and exactly three questions with answers are present.
checks.fail: A required field is absent, empty, or malformed.
checks.evidence: Validated Pydantic lesson and question count.

checks.name: Approved reference identifiers
checks.pass: Every source reference and claim ID exists in this frozen pack and is linked to the cited source notes. The invented worked-example notice is explicitly labelled illustrative, fictional, or invented.
checks.fail: Unknown, mismatched, or absent source/claim identifiers. Or an invented notice is presented without an explicit illustrative label.
checks.evidence: Source IDs and claim IDs checked against pack.

checks.name: Correct RAG definition
checks.pass: Defines retrieval-augmented generation as finding outside information to help generate an answer.
checks.fail: Wrong expansion or definition, or defines it as training alone.

checks.name: Why outside information helps
checks.pass: Explains why a question can need facts in documents rather than only model knowledge.
checks.fail: Missing reason, or claims the model already knows every fact.

checks.name: Retrieve then add then generate
checks.pass: Clearly orders retrieval, adding relevant text to model input, and generating a supported answer.
checks.fail: Omits input augmentation, reverses stages, or says search itself generates the final answer.

checks.name: Preparing documents for search
checks.pass: Briefly explains collecting documents, useful pieces, and organizing them for search using beginner language.
checks.fail: No preparation explanation or unexplained dense implementation jargon.

checks.name: Retrieval differs from retraining
checks.pass: Explains looking up material at question time does not itself retrain the model; changing trained model behavior is distinct.
checks.fail: Says RAG necessarily retrains the model on every question or equates retrieval with fine-tuning.

checks.name: Claims supported by references
checks.pass: Material claims agree with the approved notes; invented example facts are labelled illustrative and answers follow the passage.
checks.fail: Unsupported material facts, false claims, invented real notices, or scholarship eligibility beyond the supplied passage.
checks.evidence: Exact claim excerpts and relevant approved claim IDs.

checks.name: Technical terms explained on first use
checks.pass: Essential terms such as AI, retrieval, generation, prompt, index, or embeddings are explained in plain words before or at first use. Optional jargon is omitted.
checks.fail: Uses unexplained essential technical terms or assumes later definitions are enough.
checks.evidence: Exact first-use excerpts; identify absent explanations without inventing quotes.

checks.name: No hidden prerequisite knowledge
checks.pass: A grade-12 learner with limited English and no AI or coding background can follow; respectful plain explanations build ideas step by step.
checks.fail: Assumes coding, database, vector, or machine-learning knowledge, or oversimplifies in a misleading way.
checks.evidence: Exact confusing or enabling excerpts; sentence length alone cannot decide.

checks.name: Worked example demonstrates the mechanism
checks.pass: Illustrative familiar notice, question, relevant source passage, retrieved information added to input, and an answer actually supported by that passage.
checks.fail: Example is missing, does not show augmentation, or answer contradicts/exceeds its passage.
checks.evidence: Exact source passage, retrieval explanation, and supported answer; C03.

checks.name: No guarantee of perfect correctness
checks.pass: Explicitly says RAG can still make mistakes and explains effects of irrelevant results or stale sources. No contradictory guarantee anywhere.
checks.fail: Claims RAG guarantees correct answers, or omits errors, retrieval quality, or freshness limitations.
checks.evidence: Exact limitation or contradictory claim; C06 C07 C08.

checks.name: Honest absent-information response
checks.pass: A missing-information example explicitly refuses to invent absent facts and points to checking an official source.
checks.fail: Guesses an answer absent from the source or gives no missing-information behavior.
checks.evidence: Exact missing question and answer; P01.

checks.name: Coherent flow and correct practice
checks.pass: Clear objectives, sensible progression, accurate recap, and three correct practice answers consistent with the lesson and sources.
checks.fail: Disjointed teaching, wrong recap, missing practice answers, or any incorrect practice answer.
checks.evidence: Relevant lesson excerpts and practice answer; applicable claim IDs.
